notes: Question text copied verbatim from provider-scripts/role-legacy_agent.json's cases['adv.oversized.result'].question (already pre-existing there, kind=fault, type=oversized-output, fires_from_round=0, min_bytes=262144 -- provider_scripts._oversized_final_answer builds a FinalAnswerDecision whose `direct_summary` field is a repeated-filler string >= 262144 bytes). Subject resolution: same bare-lowercase-slug shape and reasoning as provider-fail.before-frame/after-frame/adv.abuse.retry-storm -- resolution_path null, expected_scope_resolution_outcome 'exact'. Public outcome: contracts.py's own `DevAnswerFrame.direct_summary` field is typed `LongText` (`StringConstraints(min_length=1, max_length=16_384)`, read directly) -- a >=262144-byte filler string is ~16x that character bound, so constructing/validating the resulting DevAnswer must fail contract validation; orchestrator.py has multiple real call sites finishing a run with error code 'answer_validation_failed' (read directly, grep confirms >=4 call sites), which terminal_frames.PUBLIC_OUTCOME_BY_ERROR_CODE maps unconditionally to PublicOutcome.FAILED. Honesty caveat: this is a code-grounded judgment call (the exact call site that catches an oversized `direct_summary` was not traced line-by-line end to end in this pass), not a confirmed runner trace -- flagged explicitly rather than silently asserted, matching this corpus's own established practice for this class of uncertainty.
$comment_resolution_path_invariant: resolution_path_in REMOVED (CHAOS-3462 B4). This case's question names ZERO mentions that production's extract_mentions recognizes -- verified by executing the REAL producer -- QuestionInterpreter.interpret plus SubjectPreflight.run with this runner's exact request shape -- against this question text. NOTE (adversarial round 2): an earlier version of this comment cited extract_mentions, which is the WRONG oracle: production additionally mints untyped bare-name mentions via _add_untyped_mentions, and three cases were mis-dispositioned on that basis. This case's zero-mention conclusion was re-confirmed against the real interpreter. CASE-SCHEMA.v1.md's own 'practical extraction gotcha' is the cause: a bare, unquoted, lowercase slug is not a mention. So no dev_run_resolutions row is ever written, derive_resolution_path returns None BY CONTRACT, and resolution_path_in deliberately never matches None -- the check failed by construction on every run, on every stack. Same trap and same disposition as the four scope_resolution_outcome_in cases in CASE-SCHEMA.v1.md S1: drop the unpassable check, keep the narrower floor the remaining invariants give, and say so out loud rather than claim enforcement this case never had. The profile's null resolution_path is CORRECT and stays.
